<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par126 />''God'' and {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים חַי|translate=the living God}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=1|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=גֻּלּתֹ עִלִּית}} and {{GHGheb|text=גּ׳ תַּחְתִּית}} are strange; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=15|verse=19}} has {{GHGheb|text=גּ׳ עִלִּיּוֹת}} and {{GHGheb|text=גּ׳ תַּחְתִּיּוֹת}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|z}}
Of the remaining examples {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=11|verse=9}} explains itself; the direct connexion of the attribute with its substantive is broken by the insertion of {{GHGheb|text=לַיָּם}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=34|verse=12}}, Hag. 1:4 (as Wellhausen says, a good instance of a Hebrew adjective in the stative form = {{GHGheb|text=וְהֵם סְפוּנִים}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=143|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=6|verse=12}} (?) the substantive is also (see above) determined by a suffix, and consequently the attribute is less closely attached; the same applies to {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=18}}, except that in these passages the omission of the article before {{GHGheb|text=ר}}, {{GHGheb|text=א}}, {{GHGheb|text=ע}} may at the same time be due to considerations of euphony (as also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=16|verse=1}} before {{GHGheb|text=ע}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=37}} before {{GHGheb|text=ר}}, 28:4, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=10|verse=9}} before {{GHGheb|text=א}}, 21:19 before {{GHGheb|text=ח}}).<ref>The same reason no doubt also favoured the omission of the article before {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫לֶּה}}, see above, under y. Also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=7}} (''is this your joyous''...?) the article is omitted before {{GHGheb|text=עַלִּיזָה}} probably only for euphony.</ref> In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=17}} f. ({{GHGheb|text=אֶחָד}}) and {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=25|verse=16}} ({{GHGheb|text=שְׁנַ֫יִם}} after a determinate substantive), the attribute again, being a numeral, is determinate in itself (see above, x); in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=65|verse=2}} the {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} prevents the use of the article; finally, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=26|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּחִצִּים}} and {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽאֲבָנִים}} are to be read, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=גֶּ֫פֶן}} for {{GHGheb|text=הַגֶּ֫פֶן}}, in 22:26 {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫רֶץ}} for {{GHGheb|text=הָאָ׳}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=6|verse=3}} omit {{GHGheb|text=חֲדָשָׁה}}, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=39|verse=27}} omit {{GHGheb|text=רַבִּים}}. Without any apparent reason the article is omitted in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=8|verse=13}} and 11:31.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|aa}}
2. When, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=12}} ({{GHGheb|text=יוֹם הוּא|translate=in that day?}}), the article is omitted from both substantive and demonstrative, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=3|verse=12}}, the demonstrative even precedes ({{GHGheb|text=זֶה חַבַּ֫יִת}}={{GHGheb|text=הַבַּ֫יִת הַזֶּה}}), this is obviously due in both cases to a radical corruption of the text (not only in the words quoted). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=9|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=לַחְמֵ֫נוּ}} is either in apposition to the independent demonstrative {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} (= ''this our bread'', &c.), as in verse 13 {{GHGheb|text=נֹאדוֹת}} is to {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫לֶּה}}, or they are complete sentences, ''this is our bread'', &c. So also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=משֶׁה}} (= ''that'' [''iste''] ''Moses'', &c.), and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=48|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} are to be taken in apposition to {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}}. On {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=8}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=13}} cf. {{GHGpar|136|d}}.<section end=par126 />

<section begin=par127 />{{GHGpar-heading|127|The Noun determined by a following Determinate Genitive}}

<div style="font-size: small; text-align: center;">Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, i. 475.</div>

{{GHGmargin-letter|127|a}}
When a genitive, determined in any way, follows a {{GHGterm|nomen regens}}, it also determines the {{GHGterm|nomen regens}}, which, according to {{GHGpar|89|a}}, is always in the construct state. Moreover, every pronominal suffix attached to a substantive is, according to {{GHGpar|33|c}}, to be considered as a genitive determinate by nature. An independent genitive may be determinate—

(''a'') By its character as a ''proper name'' (according to {{GHGpar|125|a}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=דְּבַר יְהֹוָה|translate=the word of the Lord}}.

(''b'') By having the article, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ הַמִּלְחָמָה}} (prop. the man of the war) ''the soldier'' (but {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=17|verse=1}}, ''a soldier''); {{GHGheb|text=אַנְשֵׁי הַמִּלְחָמָה}}<section end=par127 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
